RP-02 execution progress: SLICE 1 (S1 mica-governing-buck) COMPLETE AND LANDED ON MAIN; S2 and S3 remain. Session log maxixe-ironic-kiskadee (d95a-aa80-dfe0-4336) holds the full trail and an exact resume point.

LANDED (each LLM-Review +1 AND Verified +1, submitted individually per AGENTS.md's no-feature-branch fallback rather than as a 9-deep relation chain):
- 4758d47f82 / Gerrit 1880 — T1 vivacious-widish-indianabat: new binding_repository.py (360 LOC) as sole owner of live, retired, rotation and alert files.
- 1429cb8d4b / Gerrit 1885 — T2 evadable-curious-mastodon: facade delegation; binding_store.py 799 -> 710 LOC, now off the 800 cap.
- 0c318685c8 / Gerrit 1887 — T3 patterned-fossillike-betafish: ADR 0099 (289 lines) + the two uncovered publication-boundary regressions.

HELD-OUT TDD EVIDENCE. T1: 27 tests authored RED-first against a signature-only scaffold (a bare ImportError was rejected as invalid RED); the implementer saw ONLY 12 happy-path tests, with 15 fault/corruption tests physically moved out of the worktree; all 27 then passed unseen. T2 was a refactor, so RED-first is the wrong gate — characterization tests are green before and after by design, and teeth were proven by 6 defect-seeded mutations instead. Refactoring litmus applied: a behavior-preserving rename of a private helper, attribute and constant left all tests green, so they are not change-detectors.

TWO FINDINGS THE HOLD-OUT AND MUTATION CAUGHT that no visible test would have:
1. T2 mutation found a genuine ORACLE GAP: replacing the facade's alias of the repository document with a shallow copy stayed GREEN across all 27 tests, because a shallow copy still shares the inner bindings/reverse dicts — only a NEW top-level key diverges. record_comment_id's setdefault('comment_ids') on a legacy store would therefore never reach the persisted bytes, silently losing comment identity and re-posting every mirrored comment (the DIG-5301 duplicate class). Closed with an 8th test.
2. T1 validation produced 2 held-out failures that were BOTH my test defects, each verified empirically rather than assumed: two monkeypatches collided because binding_repository.os and get_rotation.os are the same stdlib module, and a dedup test was over-specified against an aspirational docstring — a differential probe proved BindingStore emits 2 alerts too, so asserting 1 would have forced a behavior change this pure extraction was forbidden from making.

Both LLM-Review advisories on T2 were applied rather than deferred; both correctly flagged change-detector coupling in my own tests (rendered-annotation assertions, and an exact ordered call trace). One Verified -1 was root-caused to a stale generated file (docs/env-vars.md line reference shifted by the refactor) and fixed; a second was traced to a KNOWN tracked macOS flake (tapestried-abhorrent-tuna closed, asbestos-popular-tench in_progress) and recheck'd with that reasoning stated per CONTRIBUTING.md section 6 — never a blind retry. That flake is now fixed on main by 9f7407bb3d.

RESIDUAL GAPS FILED SO FAR (full sweep belongs with the epic close): smalltime-rapid-elk (8384-f31f-f16f-4f14, alerts never dedupe — records omit timestamp_ns) discovered_from vivacious-widish-indianabat; best-kingly-monkey (01d8-c18d-b229-419a, retarget RP-04 S7.3.a's config reads to binding_lifecycle.py) discovered_from brainy-cooked-hog and relates_to insincere-illogical-antlion.

NEXT: S2 brainy-cooked-hog is now unblocked but UNSIGNED — run review-plan on it (only valid now that S1 is closed), then claim, then its three tasks in order 6083 -> f59b -> 2419. The session log records eight verified constraints for the remaining work, the most load-bearing being that S2 MUST re-register both moved config reads in scripts/config_ownership_exceptions.py in the same change or the pre-commit hook blocks the commit outright.
